answers.q: Is it really free?
answers.a: Yes, all of it: no plans, no trials and no limits. Nothing is sold.

answers.q: Do I need an account?
answers.a: No. You can practise on the first click. Save your progress with a passkey or an email whenever you like, so clearing this browser can't lose it.

answers.q: What does it cover?
answers.a: SAT Math: 4 domains and 19 skills, and SAT Reading and Writing vocabulary in Words. Reading and Writing questions come later.

answers.q: Can I put it on my home screen?
answers.a: Yes. In your browser's menu choose Add to Home Screen (in Safari: Share, then Add to Home Screen). It opens like an app, without the browser's bars.

answers.q: What is an open mistake?
answers.a: A named misconception you fell for, such as using the diameter as the radius. It stays open until you beat it, and every question that offers the same trap is a chance to.

answers.q: How does a mistake close?
answers.a: Two correct answers on questions that offer that same trap: right on the first try, not a guess and not an exact repeat.

answers.q: What are check-ins?
answers.a: After a mistake closes it comes back 3, 10 and 30 days later, with new numbers. Miss a check-in and the mistake opens again.

answers.q: What is a repair question?
answers.a: Right after a miss, the same kind of question with new numbers, so you fix the mistake while it's fresh. Settings can move repairs to the end of a set.

answers.q: How do I log a mistake from somewhere else?
answers.a: Press Q or tap the bolt, then Log a mistake. Type the College Board question ID, paste the question, or pick its skill. It becomes an open mistake you drill with fresh numbers.

answers.q: What does the bar under a skill mean?
answers.a: Your recent first-try answers in that skill, with harder questions counting more. It reads Learning, then Getting there, then Strong.

answers.q: Why first-try accuracy?
answers.a: Only your first answer to a question counts. Retries, repeats and guesses you tagged are left out, so the number shows what you really know.

answers.q: Will I see the same question twice?
answers.a: Not by accident: every set uses fresh numbers. Questions you save come back exactly, and Again, exactly repeats one on purpose.

answers.q: How does the practice rank work?
answers.a: Right answers over the last 7 days, among everyone, among students sitting your exam date, and in your country if you add one. Unlisted students still see their own rank.

answers.q: What are habits?
answers.a: Mistakes of one kind across different skills, like answering a different quantity than the one asked. Your profile shows your top three, each with its tell and a drill that mixes skills.

answers.q: What is test-day readiness?
answers.a: How much of the test's question types you're ready for. A type is ready once you've answered it right on the first try twice, and each type counts by how often that kind of question comes up.

answers.q: What does points on the table mean?
answers.a: How far your Math score would move if a skill reached 80% right, worked out with our score model. The model's anchors are our own stated choices, so read it as a direction and a size, not a promise.

answers.q: What does the Pace card show?
answers.a: Your time per question in each skill against how often you're right, and a drill for each case: speed up, slow down, learn it untimed, or keep it warm.

answers.q: How is my score estimated, and why a band?
answers.a: Each module or section is scored on our model of the SAT scale and shown as a band, because one sitting can't pin a score to the point. More sittings narrow it.

answers.q: What decides module 2?
answers.a: At least 60% of module 1 right (14 of 22) sends you to the harder module 2. That line is our stated choice. So a Math target above 580 needs the harder module 2, and our model tops out at 780 for a perfect paper.

answers.q: Why did my score stop at 580?
answers.a: The easier module 2 caps the section at 580. Reach the harder module 2 to go above it.

answers.q: How are grid-ins marked?
answers.a: By value: 2/3, .6666 and .6667 are all right. An answer that stops too early, like 0.66, is not: that's the SAT's fourth-digit rule.

answers.q: Can I retake a test?
answers.a: Every sitting is new: fresh questions of the same kinds, scored the same way.

answers.q: When does the score trend look ahead?
answers.a: After three scored sittings over at least three weeks. The chart then shows where the same pace would lead by your exam date, worded 'If this pace held', never as a promise.

answers.q: How does the plan choose what I do?
answers.a: It works back from your exam date and target: check-ins and open mistakes first, then the skills with the most points, with test days on the way.

answers.q: What if I miss a day?
answers.a: The plan recomputes every day, so nothing piles up.

answers.q: How does my streak work?
answers.a: A study day is a day with at least one answer, 10 word reviews or a finished test. Days in a row make the streak; rest days in your plan and spare days keep it.

answers.q: Do rest days break my streak?
answers.a: No. A rest day in your plan neither breaks your streak nor adds to it.

answers.q: What counts as study time?
answers.a: The time on every question you answer, whole tests included, word reviews and plan tasks you mark done. Each question counts at most 10 minutes.

answers.q: What is a spare day?
answers.a: Every 7 study days in a row bank one spare, up to two. Miss a study day and a spare keeps your streak going.

answers.q: What are Learn, Build and Test-like?
answers.a:
Modes that set the clock, feedback and difficulty together. With Follow my exam date on, they change by themselves: Learn until six weeks out, Build until three weeks out, then Test-like. Fixing mistakes always shows the key after each answer.
Settings › Practice holds the defaults a new set opens with. The Practice page can change them for one set, and save them as your default.

answers.q: How do I put my plan in my calendar, with reminders?
answers.a: Settings, Study, Add to calendar. Google: add the recurring event, so your own notifications apply. Apple: subscribe and untick Remove Alerts. Others: download the event, which keeps its alert. Then test it with the event two minutes from now.

answers.q: How do I use my progress on another device?
answers.a: On the other device open Sign in, then Use your phone. Scan its code with the phone that has your progress, or type its six digits under Menu, Sign in another device. A passkey or an email code works too.

answers.q: What is a passkey?
answers.a: A way to sign in with Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello or your phone: no password and no email. It syncs with your saved passwords, so it works on your other devices too.

answers.q: Can I sign in with Google?
answers.a: Where this site has Google sign-in switched on, Continue with Google shows on Sign in. We keep only your Google account id, email and name, never a Google token.

answers.q: What happens if I clear my browser?
answers.a: Unsaved progress lives only in this browser, so clearing it loses it. Save with a passkey or an email first. If the site says site data is blocked, allow site data for this site in your browser's settings.

answers.q: What is a transfer code?
answers.a: An 8-character code from Settings, Account and devices, Move to another device. Type it on the other device under Sign in, More. It works once, for 10 minutes.

answers.q: How do I sign out?
answers.a: Menu, Sign out, or Profile, Account. You get 8 seconds to undo. Settings, Account and devices signs out any device on the list.

answers.q: What does 'This is a shared computer' do?
answers.a: The sign-in lasts only this browser session: it ends 15 minutes after you stop, or about a minute after you close the browser, and nothing of yours stays on the computer.

answers.q: Can two students share one browser?
answers.a: Yes: turn on This is a family device in Settings. Each student keeps their own progress, and you switch between them in the menu, up to four.

answers.q: Why does my photo stay on this device?
answers.a: Your photo never leaves this browser: nothing uploads it. Boards and progress links show your glyph or initial instead.

answers.q: What's the difference between my name and my board name?
answers.a: Your name is private: only you see it, and anyone you send a progress link. Your board name is what boards, contests and ranks show, and nobody else can have the same one.

answers.q: Why would I add a country?
answers.a: Only for the Country board. It's blank until you choose one, and we never detect where you are.

answers.q: What happens when I report a question?
answers.a: We regenerate that exact question and check what we can at once: the numbers against an independent solver, and how strong students answer it. Anything about the wording, the figure or the options goes to a person. Our reply shows under Settings, Your reports.

answers.q: What does 'don't count this against me' do?
answers.a: While a person checks your report, that answer is left out of your accuracy, mastery and mistakes. It still counts for study time and your streak. Up to five can be open at once.

answers.q: What has been fixed from your reports?
answers.a: The latest fixes students' reports led to, newest first.

answers.q: Who sees my name?
answers.a: Only you, and anyone you send a progress link. Boards show your board name, or a student number.

answers.q: What do you store?
answers.a: Your answers and times, mistakes, saved questions, sittings, plan and preferences; your email if you save with one; your passkeys' public keys and your device list. No photo, no location and no password.

answers.q: How do I download or delete it?
answers.a: Settings, Privacy and data: Download my data gives you a file of everything, and Delete everything removes it all. Past challenge results stay on the boards as an anonymous student, so nobody else's rank changes.
